Add a CI gate for pull request texts (#268)

Add tools/check-pr-text.py, a gate that checks a pull request
description and its committed squash-message file,
.github/squash/<number>.txt. In both texts it checks review-history
labels, through the label lint loaded by file path, em and en dashes,
-ise spellings, an empty or blank text and a code fence that is never
closed; in the squash message it also checks line width, revision ids
and a subject that ends with the pull request number. The gate's
docstring states each rule, the masks and exemptions, and the exit
contract with its precondition. Add its suite,
tools/test-check-pr-text.py, with a failing case for each defect
class, cases at the edges of the masks and exemptions, cases that
compare each class of characters that ends a mask or a URL with its
set by enumeration, a mutant sweep whose sites are generated from the
gate source, and subtests on fixed probes for each form, read from
the code, that the suite's static helpers and the sweep's kill rule
accept but a plain import, whose handling changes no result, and the
workflow .github/workflows/pr-text.yml, which runs the suite and the
gate on every pull request with read-only permissions, keeps no
credentials after checkout and stops the job after 10 minutes.
tools/ci-status.py does not insist on the new check.
tools/run_all_checks.sh runs the gate's suite, and
tools/test-run-all-checks.py lists the workflow's event step as an
exception, with the suite in its place. The label lint,
tools/test-no-qa-labels.py, names the workflow in SCANNED, the files
it scans for review-history labels. The branch merged main at the
merge of pull request 273; git reported a conflict only in the
SCRIPT_SHA256 pin of tools/test-run-all-checks.py, because both sides
changed tools/run_all_checks.sh, and the pin was set to the sha256 of
the merged tools/run_all_checks.sh.

Residuals include, for example: a defect in a form the patterns miss,
such as an upper-case revision id or an -ise stem the denylist lacks;
a defect inside a masked region, or in a region the gate masks but a
renderer shows as prose, such as text glued after a URL by a comma; a
false failure on honest text that the gate reads otherwise than a
renderer shows it, such as code in an indented block; a run outside
the precondition of the exit contract, such as a label lint that ends
the gate process or replaces its standard output; a message typed
into the merge dialog that differs from the committed file; a
description edited after the last run; a change to the gate outside
the operators of the sweep, such as a change of 2 tokens at once; a
mutant whose gate never ends, which the sweep kills only by a memory
limit, a CPU limit or a wall timeout that the suite sets for each
child; the top suite process itself, which the suite does not limit
and which in CI only the job's time limit bounds; and an advisory
check, which can be merged past until the maintainer decides on
required status.
